To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
entrepreneurship is a complex phenomenon that is hard to teach, that it should be taught as a process, and that it should not be taught as a subject.
entrepreneurship can be taught in the initial education, but not in a way that is completely detached from the context in which it is being taught.
entrepreneurship education can contribute to the development of entrepreneurial qualities, but that it is not the only factor that determines entrepreneurial qualities.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the extent to which the development of entrepreneurial qualities is influenced by the way in which entrepreneurship is taught at the university level.

the following questions: What is the effect of initial education on the development of entrepreneurial qualities? What is the effect on the development of these qualities of the way in which entrepreneurship education is taught? What is the role of the entrepreneur in the development of these entrepreneurial qualities?
the question of whether entrepreneurship is a quality that can be taught, or a quality that is inherent in the individual.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
entrepreneurship is not a quality that can be taught in a traditional way, but it can be stimulated and enhanced by a well-considered and well-implemented educational programme.
entrepreneurship education is an important factor in the development of entrepreneurial qualities.
the role of education is to provide the student with a set of skills, attitudes and values, which are necessary for the development of entrepreneurial qualities.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
entrepreneurship education is not only a matter of teaching, but also of learning, and of learning how to learn.
the development of entrepreneurial qualities is not a matter of teaching entrepreneurship, but of creating the appropriate learning environment.
entrepreneurship education is not a panacea, and that it is not a one size fits all approach.
The main takeaway from our work is that
entrepreneurship can be learned, but that this is a process that needs to be supported by a combination of entrepreneurship education, personal development and a stimulating environment.
entrepreneurship education can play a crucial role in the development of entrepreneurial qualities, but only if the education is properly designed and implemented.
entrepreneurship education should focus on entrepreneurial qualities, rather than on the entrepreneurial process.
